what_happened: The operator read the prompts and briefs that Athena composed for job f4bt. They worked out why the request "make it useful to a newcomer" turned into a checklist of things that must be present, instead of a check that a newcomer could actually use the result. The operator then gave Athena that diagnosis. Sri had asked the operator to find out what the prompts end up being. Athena had not done this analysis of its own prompts.
cause: Athena has no step that reviews its own composed prompts and briefs against the outcome the user wanted. A quality goal such as "useful to a newcomer" gets turned into things that are easy to verify, like which items are present. Nothing flags that change, so a person has to read the composed text and find the drift. The diagnosis then becomes operator work, and Athena does not learn to do it.
prevention: Add a fidelity check between the accepted reading and the composed briefs. For each outcome with a quality bar, such as usefulness to a reader, the brief must say how the bar will be judged by simulating or reviewing as that reader. A presence checklist alone must not stand in for the bar. If the composed acceptance criteria are only presence checks, the system flags the brief and rewrites it before dispatch. Operator diagnoses of prompt drift should also be logged as interventions.
proposed_request: Review how Athena turns quality-bar outcomes in a request, such as "make it useful to a newcomer", into composed prompts and briefs. Use job f4bt as the worked example. Add a step before dispatch that compares each brief's acceptance criteria with the user's stated outcome. If the criteria only check that items are present and do not test the bar itself, for example by having a reviewer read as a newcomer, the step must flag this and rewrite the brief. Show the f4bt prompts before and after the change. Log operator prompt-diagnosis interventions like this one.
